text:
Andrew Peeke is in his first season in Utah after stops in Columbus and Boston, a stay-at-home defenseman playing 18 minutes a night. Eight points in 21 games is already more than half of last season's 14, and his scoring rate is well above anything his history suggests, so expect it to settle.

The more interesting number is what happens with him on the ice. Utah takes 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Peeke out there, roughly the team's rate, and the Mammoth have scored 8.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve during his shifts. That's bad luck that has cost the whole pairing, and it usually swings back.

The weaknesses are known. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season and in the bottom 10% of defensemen for creating offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found only 24% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes. On a Utah team missing Nate Schmidt, he's getting a bigger role than usual. Our talent range has him around 24 points.
